header: One row per criterion, a tick and an answer
lead: Two subjects only. The tick column is each row's included toggle; the column beside it is the sentence describing how the alternative handles the same point.
caption: Name both sides here — the column headings stay generic so the caption can carry the two real names.
note: The tick carries its own name in the markup, because a mark that means something only by its shape is unreadable to anyone using the table without seeing it.

rows.title: A covered criterion
rows.text: The sentence beside the tick says what the other side does instead.

rows.title: A criterion both sides cover
rows.text: Say so plainly. A comparison that never concedes anything is not read as a comparison.

rows.title: A criterion this option does not cover
rows.text: The cross is grey rather than red: not every gap is a failure.
